key_insight: V-DUGKS reformulates compressible flow kinetics with vectorial coupled distribution functions and second-order Hermite equilibria, enabling adjustable Prandtl number control and more stable, efficient simulation.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical finite-volume kinetic solver for continuum compressible flows that can improve accuracy and computational efficiency in shocks, instabilities, and vortex-dominated problems.
method: Couples mass, momentum, and total energy through separate relaxation processes for momentum and energy transport.
Uses second-order Hermite-truncated equilibria and fourth-order Gauss-Hermite quadrature for exact low-order moment recovery.
Applies characteristic-based flux evaluation with trapezoidal collision integration in a finite-volume DUGKS framework.
evidence_signal: The paper validates the scheme on shock-tube, Shu-Osher, 2D Riemann, and 3D Taylor-Green vortex tests, reporting about 2.2–2.9× speed-up for the 3D Taylor-Green case under the same CFL constraint.
watch_item: Performance depends on careful discrete velocity and quadrature setup, and the method is still tested primarily on benchmark problems rather than full-scale complex engineering geometries.
paper_title: Vectorial discrete unified gas kinetic scheme for continuum compressible flows
